title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — Job 1–21
description: Chapter-by-chapter study of suffering, lament, wisdom, divine justice, creation, and humility.

chapters.title: Job 1 — Job's integrity and the heavenly challenge
chapters.historicalContext: Job is introduced as a blameless and upright man; the heavenly scene frames a severe test whose purpose and limits readers must consider carefully.
chapters.overview: Job is introduced as a blameless and upright man; the heavenly scene frames a severe test whose purpose and limits readers must consider carefully.
chapters.studyObservation: Notice the movement between lament, debate, wisdom, and encounter with God. Distinguish the friends' assumptions from what the whole book ultimately affirms.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read Job 1–2 together. Follow who is speaking and how the argument develops; the book's meaning depends on the full dialogue and its conclusion.
studyQuestions: Who is speaking, and what claim or experience is being expressed?
How does this chapter develop the book's treatment of suffering, wisdom, and justice?
What harmful assumption should readers avoid when applying this passage to people in pain?
chapters.lifeApplication: Make room for honest lament, compassionate presence, intellectual humility, and care for people in suffering. Resist easy explanations that blame victims or pretend to know every reason behind hardship.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The heavenly prologue does not give humans permission to test, harm, or exploit others. Job's suffering must never be romanticized or imposed as a spiritual lesson.
chapters.readingNote: Job is wisdom literature with poetic speeches. Read each speech in context and do not treat every speaker's statement as a direct divine promise or verdict.
